(A) FLOAT CASTS: `scalar_cast_type_key` now recognizes `f16/f32/f64/f128` (new `float_scalar_cast_type_key` helper), so `expr as f32` emits the OPAQUE EUF ctor `cast:f32(<expr>)` exactly like the existing int/char casts -- no Real-arithmetic/rounding semantics in the substrate (the IEEE width rides only in the ctor NAME), location-keyed, not #euf-federated. (B) UNSAFE-BLOCK TRANSPARENCY: a single-tail `unsafe { <expr> }` (and plain `{ <expr> }`) in term position is VALUE-TRANSPARENT -- `unsafe` is a compile-time obligation, not a value transform (the same transparency `tail_inv` already applies in the value-contract path). It unwraps ONLY the single-tail shape and recurses; the inner method-call/deref/call lifts via the existing paths, so `assert_eq!(unsafe { ok.unwrap_unchecked() }, 100)` (result.rs), `unsafe { *c1.as_ptr() }`/`unsafe { *r1.as_ptr() }` (cell.rs), `unsafe { align_of_val_raw(b) }` (mem.rs) lift to the SAME term as their bare form (congruent). CRITICAL: only the WRAPPER is transparent -- `unsafe { &mut *cell.get() }` (`&mut` of a deref, not an immutable value) still BAILS through the ordinary operand path (no fake-dig of a mutable-raw deref). (C) TRY/ASYNC CONTROL-FLOW -> TERMINAL refuse (1 case): a `try {..}` / `async {..}` block or `?` (`Expr::TryBlock`/`Expr::Async`/`Expr::Try`) in term position is effectful control-flow, not a timeless point-wise value; typed as the new `ControlFlowEffect` whose reason (`effectful control-flow block`) is whitelisted TERMINAL by `refusal_disposition`.
